lines.say: [panicked, screaming] SARGE! Why is the Ogryn CARRYING me?!
lines.text: SARGE! WHY IS THE OGRYN CARRYING ME?!

lines.say: [deadpan] Orders. You're his job now, son.
lines.text: ORDERS. YOU'RE HIS JOB NOW, SON.

lines.say: [slow, dopey, proud] Sarge say protect little 'un. So Grunk protect!
lines.text: SARGE SAY PROTEKT LITTLE 'UN. SO GRUNK PROTEKT!

lines.say: [coldly] Ogryns can barely count. But they never, ever break.
lines.text: OGRYNS CAN BARELY COUNT. BUT THEY NEVER, EVER BREAK.

lines.say: [nervous] Grunk... how many Orks are coming?
lines.text: GRUNK... HOW MANY ORKS ARE COMING?

lines.say: [counting slowly, confused] One... two... um... LOTS!
[softly, tired] Fight's over, big lad. You can rest now.
lines.text: FIGHT'S OVER, BIG LAD. YOU CAN REST NOW.

lines.say: [quiet, stubborn, tired] Not till little 'un wakes up.
[moved, soft] You stayed up all night? Grunk... you're the best soldier in the Guard.
lines.text: YOU STAYED UP ALL NIGHT? GRUNK... YOU'RE THE BEST SOLDIER IN THE GUARD.

boom: Big artillery explosion, dirt raining down, war

crash: Huge brute smashing into a crowd of monsters, bodies flying, crunch and thud, comedic
roar: Crowd of brutish monsters screaming WAAAGH charging
rain: Steady night rain on metal and mud, distant thunder
birds: Quiet dawn morning, a few birds chirping, gentle wind
page: Comic book page turning quickly, paper whoosh
whoosh: Quick soft camera whoosh swipe transition

music: Heartwarming comedic military march turning gentle and emotional, snare drum, tuba, then soft strings and warm piano, instrumental, no vocals, 100 bpm
